correctness.rationale: The full frozen RESULT.md fixes a bi-infinite alternating positive-length grid and every data-independent convex adjacent-secant weight. The piecewise cubic Hermite basis has a nonnegative middle-cell derivative at all four (left,right)-slope corners; each flanking H10/H11 excursion has magnitude 4/27 and contributes 8/27 to total variation. An arbitrary finite-variation signal is a convergent sum of steps, giving a sharp column maximum. Pairing even/odd column inequalities gives a lower bound 2ab/(a^2+b^2) valid even for nonperiodic knot weights; squared-length weights u=b^2/(a^2+b^2),v=a^2/(a^2+b^2) attain it. Hence the stated minimax 1+16ab/[27(a^2+b^2)] and uniform special 35/27 follow. Independent exact rational checks recomputed the two column identities and tested 1764 two-periodic candidates across four mesh contrasts; these checks do not replace the all-index telescoping proof.

value.rationale: A natural, unbounded stability-design problem is solved over all knot-weight sequences rather than just a convenient symmetric ansatz. The exact attained minimax quantifies inevitable spline overshoot, supplies a robust coefficient prescription, and shows strong mesh contrast can improve sharp TV stability toward 1. Sharp witnesses and the telescoping impossibility bar supply structural interest beyond correct calculations; no claim to general spline optimality is made.
